newsitem.title: FRANCE: ETA's ex-leaders jailed for 10 years in France.
newsitem.headline: ETA's ex-leaders jailed for 10 years in France.

text.p: A French court on Thursday jailed three leaders of the Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA for 10 years, the maximum sentence they faced on charges of terrorist conspiracy.

The court jailed Spaniards Francisco "Pakito" Mugica Garmendia, the former operational commander of ETA, as well as explosives expert Jose Maria "Fiti" Arregui Erostarbe and ideologue Jose Luis "Txelis" Alvarez Santa Cristina.

It also jailed for 10 years Frenchman Pierre Fagant, 59, convicted of harbouring -- in the basement of his home in the southwestern French Basque region -- a clandestine ETA arms workshop producing hundreds of sub-machineguns a year.
The Paris court handed down lesser jail sentences against most of some 20 other Spanish and French defendants on charges of aiding and abetting the guerrillas.

The three ETA leaders were captured five years ago in a hideout in the French Basque region. They had been previously condemned in France on other charges, and courts have authorised their extradition to Spain once they complete serving their sentences.
Mugica Garmendia, 43, was among the most wanted men in Spain, where he is accused of sending a booby-trapped car to Madrid in 1991.
Spanish police regarded him as the operational chief of ETA, a group which has killed some 800 people in Spain in a three-decade-long campaign for a separate Basque state.

The second main defendant, Alvarez Santa Cristina, 42, is believed to have been ETA's ideologue and financier, in charge of extorting "revolutionary taxes" from businessmen in the Spanish Basque country.
The third, 50-year-old Arregui Erostarbe, was said to be the group's expert on explosives and forged identity documents.
He is wanted in Spain in connection with a parcel bomb which in 1990 badly maimed Fernando de Mateo Lage, presiding judge of the Audiencia Nacional anti-terrorist court.
